source.title: States Hidden in Hidden States: LLMs Emerge Discrete State Representations Implicitly
source.authors: Junhao Chen; Sheng-Ding Hu; Zhi-Yuan Liu; Mao-Song Sun

record.tranche_reason: The study probes arithmetic intermediate representations and their linear decodability, but does not test feature superposition, polysemanticity, or the geometry of overlapping features.
record.gate_note: The reported probe comparisons bear on representation linearity, a related but different construct, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. Arithmetic task accuracy and other IDSR results do not test the listed superposition claims.
record.test_reason: The study probes Qwen-72B and other LLMs for intermediate sums in iterative addition. It never measures feature superposition, polysemantic neurons, toy-model geometry, SAE dictionaries or feature dimensionality. Its linear-versus-MLP probe comparison concerns how decodable a task variable is, a related but different construct. The text never mentions superposition, so 'discusses' overstates it; the relation is effectively 'neither tests nor uses'.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that LLMs form implicit discrete state representations of intermediate sums at operator tokens. These representations are lossy: whole-number probe accuracy falls from 100% to 37% along the formula. They form digit by digit from the units digit up, and are built sequentially (linear, not logarithmic). An attention-bridge intervention indicates the model uses them. The authors also describe early 'shallow-semantic' versus later 'semantic' layers and a late linear-to-nonlinear shift. They draw no conclusions about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses arithmetic-state probes and attention interventions, not the original superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe results vary with layer and probe architecture; the authors also report effects of token position and prompt/task context on IDSR probing.

fits_no_version.finding: For the iterative-addition state, linear probes succeed in layers 0–50 but drop to near zero in layers 50–65, while MLP probes rise. Bottlenecked probes lose much accuracy only in layers 65–79.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intermediate arithmetic states are linearly decodable in early and middle layers but become nonlinearly encoded in late layers of large LLMs.

record.problems: The study says its experiments use only a synthetic mathematical dataset and that task diversity is unsatisfactory. The attention-mask intervention causes a substantial accuracy drop, which the authors suggest may be because the model was not trained for the modified attention pattern. Probe accuracy is indirect evidence about the representations.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweep or feature geometry.
All: no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
All: no neuron-distribution analysis or dictionary/SAE recovery.
All: the probe linearity results do not address the dimensionality of superposed features.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6 verdict is correct. The study never mentions superposition, SAEs or polysemanticity, so no verdict is given on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sparse features outnumbering dimensions are stored as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions; sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from limited capacity and features competing for dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons or recoverable with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.
Whether the features involved in superposition are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.note: The text describes this probe-accuracy trend, but it does not measure superposition or establish the dimensionality of a represented feature.
rows.check: Subject is left 'not stated'. Figure 6 does not name the model, though the paper's in-depth analyses use Qwen-72B (80 layers fits). The row measures probe capacity sensitivity, not superposition.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared single-layer and multi-layer probes for predicting digit values from hidden states.
rows.value: Single-layer probe accuracies drop to nearly zero, followed by a sharp increase for multi-layer probes.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as a transition from linear to nonlinear representations; this does not establish that features are superposed one-dimensional directions.
rows.check: Same subject issue as R1. The linear-to-nonlinear decodability shift concerns a task variable's probe-linearity, not whether superposed features are 1-D directions (V6).
